name: Certified in Cybersecurity
focus: Security principles, business continuity, access controls, network security, and security operations.
notes: Entry-level ISC2 credential for people starting a cybersecurity path.

name: Security+
focus: Core cybersecurity, risk, architecture, operations, and governance.
notes: Baseline SOC credential; verify regional voucher pricing before purchase.

name: GSEC
focus: Practical security fundamentals, defense, networking, cryptography, Linux, Windows, and incident handling basics.
notes: Hands-on security fundamentals credential aligned with SANS training.

name: Microsoft Security Operations Analyst Associate
focus: Microsoft Sentinel, Defender XDR, Defender for Cloud, KQL, threat detection, and response.
notes: Best fit for SOCs using Microsoft Sentinel and Defender.

name: CySA+
focus: Security analytics, detection, vulnerability management, incident response, and reporting.
notes: Strong fit for blue-team analysts and SOC progression after Security+.

name: GCIH
focus: Incident handling, attacker techniques, detection, response, containment, and remediation.
notes: Strong incident response credential for SOC/CSIRT analysts.

name: GCIA
focus: Network traffic analysis, intrusion detection, packet interpretation, and traffic-based threat hunting.
notes: Good fit for network detection and packet-analysis-heavy SOC roles.

name: AWS Certified Security - Specialty
focus: AWS identity, logging, monitoring, infrastructure security, data protection, and incident response.
notes: Best fit for cloud security roles in AWS-heavy environments.

name: CCSP
focus: Cloud architecture, cloud data security, platform security, application security, operations, and legal risk.
notes: Good fit for cloud security engineers and security architects.

name: CISA
focus: IT audit, governance, systems acquisition, operations, resilience, and protection of information assets.
notes: Best fit for audit, compliance, assurance, and risk roles.

name: CISM
focus: Information security governance, risk management, program development, incident management, and leadership.
notes: Good management-track certification for security leaders and program owners.

name: CISSP
focus: Security and risk management, asset security, architecture, operations, IAM, testing, and software security.
notes: Widely recognized senior cybersecurity certification. Requires experience endorsement after passing.

name: GCFA
focus: Digital forensics, incident response, endpoint artifacts, timeline analysis, and threat hunting.
notes: Strong forensics and DFIR credential for advanced responders.

name: PenTest+
focus: Penetration testing, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, reporting, and remediation guidance.
notes: Useful for analysts moving toward offensive security or validation testing.

name: CEH
focus: Ethical hacking methodology, reconnaissance, scanning, exploitation concepts, and security testing.
notes: Well-known HR-filter certification. Compare against hands-on options if the role is technical.

name: OSCP
focus: Hands-on penetration testing, exploitation, privilege escalation, Active Directory attacks, and reporting.
notes: Practical offensive-security certification with a strong hands-on reputation.

name: SecurityX
focus: Enterprise security architecture, engineering, governance, risk, and advanced operations.
notes: Previously CASP+. Better aligned to senior technical security roles than entry-level SOC work.

name: A+
focus: Computer hardware, operating systems, software troubleshooting, networking, security, and technical support.
notes: Broad starting credential for help desk, desktop support, and early IT operations roles.

name: Network+
focus: Network architecture, implementation, operations, troubleshooting, and security fundamentals.
notes: Vendor-neutral networking baseline for infrastructure and security careers.

name: Linux+
focus: Linux administration, security, scripting, containers, troubleshooting, and operational automation.
notes: Vendor-neutral Linux credential useful for system administration and security operations.

name: Server+
focus: Server installation, administration, storage, security, disaster recovery, and troubleshooting.
notes: Infrastructure credential for administrators supporting physical and virtual server environments.

name: Cloud+
focus: Cloud architecture, deployment, operations, security, DevOps fundamentals, and troubleshooting.
notes: Vendor-neutral cloud operations credential spanning multiple deployment models.

name: CCNA
focus: Network fundamentals, IP connectivity, network access, security fundamentals, automation, and programmability.
notes: Widely recognized networking credential for infrastructure and security practitioners.

name: Cisco CyberOps Associate
focus: Security monitoring, host and network analysis, intrusion investigation, and incident response procedures.
notes: Cisco blue-team credential aligned with entry and intermediate SOC analyst work.

name: Cisco CyberOps Professional
focus: Advanced threat hunting, incident response, forensic analysis, automation, and security operations leadership.
notes: Advanced Cisco SOC credential for experienced analysts and incident responders.

name: CCNP Security
focus: Enterprise security architecture, network security, identity, secure access, VPNs, content security, and automation.
notes: Professional-level Cisco credential for implementing and operating enterprise security controls.

name: Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals
focus: Security, compliance, identity concepts, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft security and compliance solutions.
notes: Entry Microsoft credential for learners beginning a security, identity, or compliance path.

name: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
focus: Cloud concepts, Azure architecture and services, governance, management, pricing, and support.
notes: Foundational Azure credential for technical and nontechnical cloud learners.

name: Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator Associate
focus: Microsoft Entra identities, authentication, access management, workload identities, and identity governance.
notes: Role-based Microsoft credential for identity administrators and IAM engineers.

name: Microsoft Cybersecurity Architect Expert
focus: Zero Trust strategy, governance, security operations, identity, infrastructure, applications, and data security architecture.
notes: Expert credential requiring an eligible Microsoft security associate certification plus SC-100.

name: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
focus: AWS cloud concepts, core services, security and compliance, billing, pricing, and support.
notes: Foundational AWS credential for understanding cloud services and the shared responsibility model.

name: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate
focus: Designing secure, resilient, high-performing, and cost-optimized distributed systems on AWS.
notes: Core AWS architecture credential that provides strong context for cloud security work.

name: AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer - Associate
focus: Deploying, managing, monitoring, securing, and troubleshooting workloads and services on AWS.
notes: Operations-focused AWS credential formerly named SysOps Administrator - Associate.

name: Google Cloud Digital Leader
focus: Cloud concepts, Google Cloud products, digital transformation, trust, security, operations, and business value.
notes: Foundational Google Cloud credential with no technical prerequisite.

name: Google Associate Cloud Engineer
focus: Deploying and securing infrastructure, managing cloud solutions, monitoring operations, and configuring access.
notes: Hands-on Google Cloud operations credential for deploying and maintaining cloud projects.

name: Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer
focus: Identity, network defense, data protection, security operations, automation, compliance, and secure cloud workloads.
notes: Advanced Google Cloud credential for designing and operating secure cloud environments.

name: Google Professional Security Operations Engineer
focus: Security monitoring, detection engineering, threat hunting, incident response, and Google security operations tooling.
notes: Role-based Google Cloud certification for advanced security operations practitioners.

name: SSCP
focus: Access controls, security operations, risk identification, incident response, cryptography, networks, and systems security.
notes: Practitioner-focused ISC2 credential for implementing and operating security controls.

name: CGRC
focus: Governance, risk management, control assessment, authorization, continuous monitoring, and compliance frameworks.
notes: ISC2 credential for practitioners applying risk management and authorization frameworks.

name: CSSLP
focus: Secure software lifecycle, requirements, architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, and supply-chain security.
notes: Advanced secure-development credential for software and application security professionals.

name: CRISC
focus: IT risk identification, assessment, response, mitigation, control design, monitoring, and reporting.
notes: Risk-focused credential for practitioners connecting technology risk with business objectives.

name: CDPSE
focus: Privacy governance, privacy architecture, data lifecycle management, and privacy engineering controls.
notes: Technical privacy credential for designing and operating privacy-protective systems.

name: GCTI
focus: Cyber threat intelligence collection, analysis, attribution, intelligence requirements, and strategic reporting.
notes: Specialist credential for analysts producing operational and strategic threat intelligence.

name: GREM
focus: Malware reverse engineering, behavioral analysis, code analysis, document malware, and malicious software reporting.
notes: Advanced hands-on credential for malware analysts and reverse engineers.

name: GNFA
focus: Network forensics, packet analysis, flow records, log correlation, encrypted traffic, and incident reconstruction.
notes: Network-forensics credential for responders investigating activity across packet and log evidence.

name: GPEN
focus: Penetration testing methodology, reconnaissance, exploitation, password attacks, web testing, and reporting.
notes: GIAC penetration-testing credential covering enterprise attack techniques and reporting.

name: GWAPT
focus: Web application reconnaissance, authentication attacks, injection, client-side attacks, APIs, and testing methodology.
notes: Specialist credential for web application and API penetration testing.

name: GDSA
focus: Defense-in-depth architecture, zero trust, network segmentation, cloud security, identity, and resilient design.
notes: Architecture credential for senior defenders designing layered enterprise security controls.

name: Splunk Core Certified Power User
focus: Searching, reporting, knowledge objects, field aliases, lookups, macros, data models, and workflow actions.
notes: Practical starting credential for analysts who search and report in Splunk.

name: Splunk Enterprise Certified Admin
focus: Splunk Enterprise configuration, data ingestion, indexing, user management, distributed search, and platform monitoring.
notes: Administration credential for operating enterprise Splunk environments and data pipelines.

name: Splunk Certified Cybersecurity Defense Analyst
focus: Threat detection, investigation, risk-based alerting, threat intelligence, incident response, and Splunk security workflows.
notes: Splunk security credential designed for SOC and defensive analysis workflows.

name: Red Hat Certified System Administrator
focus: Enterprise Linux administration, storage, users, services, networking, security, shell scripting, and containers.
notes: Performance-based Linux administration credential with direct relevance to security operations.

name: Red Hat Certified Engineer
focus: Enterprise Linux automation, configuration management, deployment, administration, and Ansible-based operations.
notes: Advanced performance-based Linux engineering credential built on current RHCSA skills.

name: Red Hat Certified Specialist in Security: Linux
focus: Linux security hardening, access controls, encrypted storage, intrusion detection, compliance scanning, and remediation.
notes: Performance-based specialist credential for securing Red Hat Enterprise Linux systems.

name: Certified Kubernetes Administrator
focus: Kubernetes cluster architecture, installation, networking, workloads, storage, troubleshooting, and security administration.
notes: Performance-based Kubernetes administration credential useful for cloud and container security roles.
